subject: general
question:
Study the given graph showing the rainfall (in mm) in three cities, i.e. Delhi, Mumbai and Chennai from the year 2000 to 2003 and answer the question that follows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f89d0773b8d51f9c33e4d3c4e88130510f101e32fbe69856d51343be600304be.png] 

What is the highest percentage of increase or decrease in average rainfall in a particular year in comparison to its previous year?
solution:
**Calculation:**

Total rainfall in year 2000 (in mm) = 50 + 70 + 90 = 210

Average rainfall in year 2000 = 210 / 3 = 70 mm

Total rainfall in year 2001 (in mm) = 70 + 90 +80 = 240

Average rainfall in year 2001 = 240 / 3 = 80 mm

Total rainfall in year 2002 (in mm) = 110 + 80 + 140 = 330

Average rainfall in year 2002 = 330 / 3 = 110 mm

Total rainfall in year 2003 (in mm) = 60 + 130 + 80 = 270

Average rainfall in year 2003 = 270 / 3 = 90 mm

Increase in average rainfall from 2000 to 2001 = 80 - 70 = 10

% in increase is given by:

⇒ (10 / 70) × 100

⇒ 14.28 % increase

Increase in average rainfall from 2001 to 2002 = 110 - 80 = 30

% in increase is given by:

⇒ (30 / 80) × 100

⇒ 37.50 % increase

Decrease in average rainfall from 2002 to 2003 = 110 - 90 = 20

% in decrease is given by:

⇒ (20 / 110) × 100

⇒ 18.18 % decrease

**So, the highest percentage of increase in average rainfall is in 2002 as compared to 2001 and the percentage increase is 37.50%.**
